decision: routed to figure-it-out with high rigor
why: public API change plus safety claims on an asm parser; mistakes there are crashes or wrong trees for every caller

decision: done means: no writable static data in libtsasm.a; per-call parser handle; libFuzzer+ASan+guard pages and valgrind find nothing; stress suite passes; parity >= 6424/6464 with no new mismatch kinds; single-thread speed within 5% of baseline; scaling table vs C at 1/6/12/20 workers
why: falsifiable predicate before starting

decision: read parser.s: all mutable state is one .bss ctx reached through r15; lexer and tables are register-only and read-only
why: r15-relative layout means reentrancy is mostly swapping lea r15,[rip+ctx] for a caller pointer

decision: found unbounded native recursion in p_subtree_compare and O(depth) stack copies/scans per fork/converge outside the step budget
why: deep nesting can overflow a thread stack, and pathological forks can make time quadratic despite the advance budget

decision: no clang on the machine; extracted clang-18 debs into ~/Storage/tools/clang18 (no sudo); libFuzzer+ASan smoke test caught a planted overflow
why: fuzzing needs libFuzzer; installed llvm-18 compiler-rt already had the runtime

decision: API: opaque TsasmParser, parser_new/free/set_memory_limit, tsasm_parse_go(p, src, len, const TsasmNode **nodes) returning count or -1 syntax / -3 limit / -4 out of memory; parser owns the output array
why: an independent design agent proposed two shapes and picked parser-owned output; it removes the -2 retry-and-reparse protocol and puts output memory inside the one budget
evidence: design agent reply (Candidate A vs B vs C) in session transcript

decision: dropped from the agent's proposal: TsasmLimits struct, steps/depth/input knobs, BUSY flag, trim and last_error calls
why: no caller needs them; memory budget subsumes depth and input caps; one-call-at-a-time per parser is the same contract as TSParser

decision: retention: free buffers at the start of a parse when the parser holds more than 64 MiB, not at the end
why: the output array must stay valid after the call returns

decision: moved ctx to heap TsasmParser, one p_grow helper with memory accounting and capacity stored after realloc, iterative subtree compare, work charges for copies and convergence scans, -3/-4 codes
why: the four defects the design agent and I both found; one helper instead of four copies so the accounting rule lives in one place
evidence: commit 99e61e3, test/check_all on f200.txt: 199/200 same as baseline

decision: user asked mid-run for multiple grammars: make the runtime language-generic and prove it on go, c, java, json (the local grammars with no external scanner)
why: user request; c and java break the <=128-token assumption and json has no keyword lexer, so they exercise the generalization

decision: language passed per call: tsasm_parse(p, lang, src, len, &nodes); generator emits one asm file per grammar exporting only tsasm_language_<name>(); runtime copies the descriptor into the parser context at parse start
why: per-call language leaves no 'language not set' state; copying keeps every table access one load off r15 instead of rip-relative

decision: deleted the C model (test/model.c), its speed tools and dbg/reftrace/lexwrap
why: parity is checked against C tree-sitter itself; the model was a second reference that every API change had to track

decision: gen.py: an eof edge in a lexer state is guarded only if it lies on a cycle of eof edges
why: guarding every eof edge broke JSON/C/Java (edges that lead to the accept state); only cycles can spin at eof; all four grammars have 0 guarded edges

decision: corpora: Go = GOROOT 1.22 src (test/files.txt); C = 8732 files from /usr/include, ~/go/pkg/mod, Go src; Java = Guava (3267 files); JSON = 2539 files
why: largest local sources per grammar; file lists committed under corpus/

decision: Java GLR: versions C holds as one merged head (same state and position, not convertible) form a group; inside a group convergence picks by subtree compare instead of keeping X for an equivalent node; groups re-form at every condense; forks by action k get ids derived from k
why: C keeps both links and picks by ts_subtree_compare at the reduce that rejoins them; Java 297 mismatches were all method_reference after '::' (identifier vs type_identifier)

decision: rejected: grouping any pair C merges (Go 39->81 mismatches, C 2->16), and emulating C's head merge by rewriting Y's upper entries (Go 295)
why: C's merged heads create path combinations no single version holds (repro gr/17.go: C.f(u.P(u.P(c)))); exact emulation needs a graph-structured stack

decision: only pairs that were one head last condense, or both ungrouped, may join a group
why: keeps Go exactly at baseline while fixing most of Java
evidence: results/parity_*.txt: go 6424/39 identical details, c 3554/2, json 2529/0, java 3254->3235 match, 19 mismatch

decision: fuzz harness: libFuzzer (LLVM 18 compiler-rt, linked with gcc/g++ since no clang binary is installed); asm coverage via an 8-bit counter after every label (scripts/covinstr.py); asm buffers and the input in guard-page allocations; ASan on the harness and C reference; oracles: output contract, determinism across parsers, allocation-failure injection then clean reparse, low memory limit, and never accept what C rejects
why: ASan cannot see the asm's loads; guard pages can. A differential accept oracle catches lexer and table bugs that do not crash

decision: fuzz round 1 (8 jobs, ~47 active min, ~600k execs): 2 real bugs. (1) tsl_set_contains took its count in ecx, the lexer's accepted-symbol register: a non-ASCII lookahead that failed a set test after an accept returned the count as the token symbol (pre-existing in the baseline generator). (2) a token accepted before skipped whitespace had start > end; C resets start to end (ts_lexer_finish). Plus 1 harness bug (Go's NUL token is named "\\0")
why: both found by the never-accept-what-C-rejects and span oracles; reproduced and fixed at the root
evidence: fuzz/regress/*, make fuzz-regress passes; parities unchanged

decision: scaling, go1.26.5 src (7710 files, 90.3 MB), fuzzers paused, 5 runs each: asm 70.8/405.7/605.2/758.1 MB/s at 1/6/12/20 workers; C 8.7/53.7/83.8/101.2
why: same session, interleaved per worker count; work counters equal per pass

decision: limiter: pinned layouts with busy-CPU clock sampling. Per-GHz throughput holds from 1 to 6 P-cores (18.7 -> 20.2 MB/s/GHz/worker); SMT adds 38% per core; E-core = 0.80x P per GHz; at 20 workers the clock drops to P 3.19 / E 2.53 GHz and measured 767 MB/s = 94% of the per-GHz model (C: 99%)
why: asm scaling is set by core-GHz (package power limit, SMT, E-cores), not by shared software state or memory
